faq: Do I have to verify before users can log in?
It is your choice. Some products allow limited use right away and ask for verification later, which keeps sign-up smooth. We build the rule you prefer.
Your own email service, such as Postmark, SendGrid, Amazon SES or Resend. If you have none, we suggest an inexpensive one and set it up in your own account.
Why might verification emails not arrive?
Common causes are a missing sender setup or strict spam filters. We check your sender settings and the message content. Inbox placement is controlled by the providers, so we cannot promise it.
Can you add this to existing users?
Yes. We can mark current users as verified or ask them to verify at their next login. You choose, and we explain what each option means for support.
desc:
Email verification and welcome emails for new users confirm that every sign-up address is real and point people to their first step. Ecom Swift LLC adds a one-use verification link and a clear welcome message to your own app's sign-up flow.

## What is email verification?

Email verification is a step at sign-up where the user proves that they own the address they typed. The app sends a short message with a one-use link. When the user clicks it, the account is marked as verified and the person returns to your product.

It is a small feature with a large effect on how clean your user list stays. Without it, any typo or invented address becomes a permanent record.

## Why unverified addresses cause problems

A mistyped address means the user never receives your receipts, reset links or product news. They assume your app is broken and write to support, or they leave. A made-up address creates a fake account that nobody owns.

There are technical costs too. Sending mail to addresses that do not exist produces bounces, and a high bounce volume can harm how mailbox providers treat your sending domain. Real messages may then land in spam for everyone.

## How verification and a good welcome improve your results

Verification protects delivery. Once you know an address works, every later email, from invoices to password resets, has a better chance of arriving. It also reduces abuse, because creating throwaway accounts takes more effort.

The welcome email matters for activation. A new user who sees a short message with one clear first action is more likely to come back than one who gets silence. The email works because it arrives when interest is highest and tells people exactly what to do next, in your own voice.

## What a great setup includes

- A verification email with one clear button and a plain-text fallback.
- A one-use link that stops working after it has been clicked.
- A saved verified status on the account, not only a session flag.
- A resend button with a short wait, so it cannot be spammed.
- A visible notice in the app until the address is confirmed.
- An expired-link page that offers a fresh link instead of an error.
- Verification again when a user changes their email.
- Limits on certain features until the address is verified.
- A welcome email that names the first thing to do.
- Handling for bounced and blocked addresses.

## What we do

We add the verification step to your existing sign-up, using the email service you already have or one you choose. We build the waiting screen, the resend control and the expired-link page, and we test the odd cases: a link opened twice, a link opened on another device, and a user who changes their address mid-way.

Then we write the emails with you. The Basic package covers the link, the saved status, resend and the notice. Standard adds branded emails, a welcome message, feature limits and expiry handling. Premium adds a short onboarding series written for your product, a review of sender and domain settings, bounce handling and a report of verified and unverified users.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Keep the verification email short with a single action.
- Tell users where to look if the message does not arrive.
- Let people correct a mistyped address without starting over.
- Send the welcome email only after verification is complete.
- Use a sender name your users recognize.

**Avoid:**
- Blocking the whole app with no explanation while waiting.
- Links that never expire or can be used many times.
- Welcome emails that list every feature instead of one first step.
- Sending from a domain with no authentication records set up.
- Treating existing users the same as new ones without a plan.

## Who this is for

It suits a new SaaS product that is collecting sign-ups with typos and fake addresses in the list. It also fits a business whose mailing provider warns about bounces, or a team that has verification but only a plain default email. Apps with trial periods benefit too, since a verified address is how you reach people before the trial ends.

## What we need from you

Send us your brand name, logo and tone notes, plus the email service you use or want to use. Please add us to the project as a collaborator or developer user, with a test environment to work in. We never need passwords. If you already have users, tell us how you want them handled, since the choice between asking them to verify or marking them as verified is yours.
